title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Ship attacks are spreading from Hormuz into the wider Gulf, with 32 strikes around the Arabian Peninsula so far in October and a tug hit off Khor Fakkan, while 383 ships wait at anchor off the UAE. On land, Khorfakkan is racing to 5 million TEU of capacity this month and Saudi air links are still not back to normal.

stories.headline: Attacks spread from Hormuz into the wider Gulf, and a tug is hit off Khor Fakkan
body: Two more tankers were struck on 20 and 21 October, one 11 nautical miles west of Bukha in Oman and one southeast of Al Faw in Iraq. Crews are safe. On 18 October a tug about 20 nautical miles northeast of Khor Fakkan was hit by two projectiles. The shipping security centre JMIC has raised the threat level for the wider Persian Gulf to "substantial" and keeps Hormuz at "severe".

About 217 ships were anchored off Fujairah and Khor Fakkan on 18 October, with 166 more between Dubai and Ras Al Khaimah. UKMTO counts 32 attacks around the Arabian Peninsula so far in October, double September's 16.
stories.soWhat: New this week: the risk now reaches the UAE's east-coast approaches, not just the strait. Keep war-risk surcharges in place and warn shippers that east-coast routings also carry delay risk.

stories.headline: Khorfakkan doubles down as the Gulf's bypass port
body: Gulftainer is spending $2 billion to take Khorfakkan to 10 million TEU a year. The first phase, to 5 million TEU, is due by the end of October. Weekly throughput has already jumped from about 8,000 TEU to 65,000 TEU, the terminal's current limit.

Inland, the Sajaa dry port and the Al Dhaid hub, built to link to Etihad Rail, add 2.3 million TEU of capacity. The Gemini alliance's Far East–Middle East loop (Maersk FM1, Hapag-Lloyd AGX) now calls Khor Fakkan instead of Jebel Ali, and Maersk and Kuehne+Nagel flag berth congestion there.
stories.soWhat: Khorfakkan is where Gulf import boxes will land for months. Our freight, customs and trucking offer from Khor Fakkan and Sajaa to Dubai and KSA needs to be priced and sold as a product.

stories.headline: Gulf shipping now costs five times prewar levels
body: The IEA says shipping Gulf crude to Asia costs over $37 a barrel, more than five times prewar. A typical supertanker cargo now pays over $74 million in freight, against under $15 million before the war.
Oil keeps moving despite the attacks: flows through Hormuz are about 82% of prewar, and 40% of Gulf crude exports now bypass the strait, up from about 17%.
stories.soWhat: Energy shipping costs feed straight into bunker and fuel surcharges. Expect carrier fuel charges to stay high through Q4.

stories.headline: UAE airlines' Riyadh flights still cancelled after the airport reopens
body: On Tuesday's schedule, Emirates (EK819/820), flydubai (FZ847/848) and Etihad (EY555/556) Riyadh flights were all cancelled. Air Arabia's Sharjah–Riyadh flights stay off with no restart date. Flights in and out of Riyadh need permission from Saudi civil aviation, per Reuters.
What is new: Emirates' planned return to Riyadh on 20 October did not show on the day. Saudi carriers Saudia, flynas, flyadeal and Riyadh Air are flying.
stories.soWhat: UAE belly space into Riyadh is still not reliable. Keep road as the default for KSA and quote air on Saudi carriers only where speed matters.

stories.headline: Fuel is rising faster than air rates into peak
body: Jet fuel was up 111% year on year in the week to 9 October, per IATA. The global Baltic air freight index fell 2.1% in the week to 12 October but is still 24.3% above last year.
Analyst David Kerr warned that "fuel costs were rising faster than freight rates". AI hardware shippers that have not yet booked peak space could push rates sharply higher.
stories.soWhat: Margin risk sits in fuel, not base rates. Make sure our air fuel surcharge tracks weekly jet fuel.

stories.headline: Al Sharqi opens a Dh70m cold-chain hub in Dubai Industrial City
body: Al Sharqi Shipping has opened a multi-temperature hub with 280,000 sq ft of storage, from ambient to minus 18°C. It has 38 loading lanes, handles up to 178 trucks a day and lifts the company to 37,800 pallet positions.
It targets food, FMCG, retail, HoReCa, quick commerce and manufacturing. Dubai Industrial City has an Etihad Rail freight terminal.
stories.soWhat: More cold storage is coming to Jebel Ali's doorstep. Pitch our cold-chain last mile to the shippers who will use it.

stories.headline: JD.com's property arm plans a 2.5m sq ft Dubai fulfilment hub
body: Gargash Prime and JINGDONG Property, JD.com's infrastructure arm, signed an MoU on 13 October to form a joint venture. They plan a regional distribution and fulfilment hub of about 2.5 million sq ft in Dubai.
No site, start date or tenants have been named yet.
stories.soWhat: A Chinese e-commerce giant is building Gulf fulfilment scale. Get in early on its last-mile and cross-border needs.

competitors.name: DHL
competitors.headline: DHL raises guidance as express profit jumps
body: DHL Group lifted its 2026 EBIT outlook to more than €7 billion, from €6.5 billion. Q3 revenue was about €22.6 billion, up over 12%.
DHL Express Q3 EBIT was about €1,035 million, against €692 million a year ago. About €100 million came from tight airfreight capacity. DHL credits "yield and cost measures" and weight growth.
competitors.soWhat: The market leader is making money from yield, not volume. That supports firm pricing from us, not discounting, through peak.
competitors.imageCredit: DHL Express via Air Cargo News

competitors.name: FedEx
competitors.headline: FedEx takes dangerous goods by road across five GCC markets
body: FedEx now moves eligible dangerous goods by road from its Dubai World Central hub to Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, Kuwait and Oman. It covers lab reagents, diagnostic samples, dry ice, chemicals and lithium batteries, with day-definite, customs-cleared delivery.
The DWC hub also won IATA CEIV Pharma certification on 9 October. It has 57,000 sq m with a 170 sq m temperature-controlled area.
competitors.soWhat: FedEx is going after healthcare and battery shippers who cannot fly into KSA right now. Match it with a DG and pharma road product of our own.

competitors.name: Emirates Courier Express
competitors.headline: Emirates' courier arm signs Dubai online brands
body: Emirates Courier Express is promoting wins with Dubai sellers: activewear brand Squatwolf, Shopify fulfilment firm Mayple Global and Magrabi Optical, which moves eyewear across the GCC.
Squatwolf says it has seen "a meaningful reduction in customer complaints" on delivery times.
competitors.soWhat: Emirates is targeting our core: Dubai D2C brands shipping cross-border. Protect key e-commerce accounts with transit-time guarantees.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: Our latest figure: record Q2 revenue
body: Aramex reported Q2 2026 revenue of AED 1.83 billion, up 22%, its highest ever. Net profit was AED 47.4 million, against a reported loss a year earlier.
Freight forwarding posted record revenue on pricing discipline. Domestic express grew, and international express volumes were broadly stable.
competitors.soWhat: DHL's express jump sets the bar for our Q3. Freight is our strongest card while sea lanes are disrupted.

opportunities.title: Khorfakkan gateway product
opportunities.text: Capacity there heads to 5m TEU this month and Gemini now calls there. Sell port-to-door from Khor Fakkan and Sajaa to Dubai and KSA.

opportunities.title: Road to KSA while air is patchy
opportunities.text: UAE airlines' Riyadh flights are still cancelled. Road express and freight into Saudi stays the reliable option.

opportunities.title: Cold chain near Jebel Ali
opportunities.text: New cold storage at Dubai Industrial City brings FMCG and quick-commerce shippers who need cold last mile.

opportunities.title: JD.com's Dubai hub
opportunities.text: A 2.5m sq ft fulfilment hub is planned. Pitch early for last-mile and cross-border work.

opportunities.title: Healthcare and DG by road
opportunities.text: FedEx's move shows demand for GCC road DG and pharma. We can compete on network depth.

watchouts.title: Attacks near the east coast
watchouts.text: A tug was hit off Khor Fakkan and the wider Gulf threat level is up. East-coast routings are not risk-free.

watchouts.title: Port queues
watchouts.text: 383 ships at anchor off the UAE and berth congestion at Khor Fakkan. Transit promises need buffers.

watchouts.title: Fuel outrunning rates
watchouts.text: Jet fuel up 111% and tanker costs five times prewar. Fixed-rate contracts lose margin fast.

watchouts.title: Emirates in our e-commerce base
watchouts.text: Emirates Courier Express is signing Dubai D2C brands with its own lift.

watchouts.title: UPS results on 27 October
watchouts.text: Another price and surcharge signal is coming. Be ready to respond.

moves.title: Launch a Khorfakkan port-to-door offer
moves.text: Package customs, Sajaa storage and trucking to Dubai and KSA, with a published rate, for importers rerouted off Jebel Ali.

moves.title: Hold war-risk and add delay terms for east-coast cargo
moves.text: The threat now reaches Khor Fakkan's approaches. Keep surcharges and add delay clauses on sea-air and sea-road quotes.

moves.title: Index air fuel surcharge weekly
moves.text: Jet fuel is up 111% year on year. Move our air fuel surcharge to weekly jet fuel, not monthly.

moves.title: Keep KSA on road and tell customers
moves.text: UAE airlines' Riyadh flights are still off. Confirm road transit times to key accounts and offer air only on Saudi carriers.

moves.title: Lock in top D2C accounts
moves.text: Offer transit-time guarantees and volume tiers to Dubai online brands before Emirates Courier Express calls them.

moves.title: Build a GCC road DG and pharma product
moves.text: Answer FedEx with day-definite DG and temperature-controlled road service to KSA, Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman.
